Overview of COVID-19
Academic Impact Study

Introduction
Components
• Provide context of COVID-19 in Indiana & nationally
• Identify state & federal expectations
• Acknowledge “pre-existing” conditions
• Indicate purpose/s of study
• Understand academic impact of COVID-19 to provide intentional supports &
resources
• NOT accountability

Research Questions
• Question #1: Who are the students in Indiana?
• Overall description of student population.
• Overall description of students for whom assessment data has been collected. Who do we
not have data?

• Question #2: To what extent did COVID-19 disruptions impact student
academic performance & learning outcomes?
• Overall academic impact
• Disparities in academic impact
• Content area academic impact (E/La & math; English language proficiency)

• Question #3: What is the anticipated academic recovery time based on
the experienced COVID-19 disruptions?

Research Questions
Areas of Consideration
• Student racial/ethnic subgroup
• Special education status
• English learner status
• Poverty status
• Community type (urban, suburban, rural)
• School type (traditional public, charter, nonpublic/choice)
• Mode of instruction
• Student attendance

Data Sources
Components
• Assessment data
• ILEARN for E/La & math (grades 3-8)
• WIDA ACCESS 2.0 for English learners (K-12)
• NWEA MAP interim for E/La & math (grades 1-10)
• Population data
• Ed-Fi Attendance & Student Demographic data
• Poverty index data
• Technology data
• Annual technology plan

Data Sources
Notes on NWEA MAP data
• Received data from Fall 2020-2021 and Winter 2020-2021 administration
windows
• Data consisted primarily of language arts and mathematics data for Grades
• Statewide participation approached/exceeded 40% in all grades except 9 & 10

Notes on High School data
• Limited interim assessment data makes it difficult to conduct sufficient
analysis of grades 9-12
• Changes in ISTEP+ 10 administration introduce problems for comparison of
status & growth.

Methodology
Components
• Consultation with Indiana Technical Advisory Committee
• Measurement of academic impact
• Status: comparison of proficiency level from year to year
• Growth: comparison of growth (cohort referenced and baseline) from year to year
• Measurement of recovery time
• No Impact
• Minor Impact
• Moderate Impact
• Significant Impact

Methodology
Measurement of Academic Impact – NWEA Interim
Assessment
• Consider status & growth comparisons of the following:
• Fall 19/20 to Fall 20/21
• Fall 20/21 to Winter 20/21
• Winter 19/20 to Winter 20/21
• Fall 20/21 to Spring 20/21
• Winter 20/21 to Spring 20/21
• Spring 18/19 to Spring 20/21

Methodology
Measurement of Academic Impact – Summative
Assessment
• Consider status & growth comparisons of the following:
• Spring 2019 to Spring 2021

Measurement of Academic Impact – WIDA ACCESS 2.0
Assessment
• Consider status & growth comparisons of the following:
• Winter 2020 to Winter 2021

Findings
Components
• Enrollment, attendance, and mode of instruction, broken out by sub-
topics
• Experienced learning loss, broken out by sub-topics
• Disparities in learning loss, broken out by sub-topics
• Content area learning loss, broken out by sub-topics
• Assigned recovery time “impact” statuses, broken out by sub-topics

Conclusion & Recommendations
Components
• Summary of COVID-19 academic impact
• Policy & support interventions
• Theory of action—identify purpose/priorities/goals for accelerating
learning
• Divide into short-term/immediate need & long-term strategy based
on establishment of “baseline” and current “impact” category
• Ensure equity considerations of “pre-existing conditions” are
considered in any strategic planning

Timeline
Components
• May/June 2021
• Receive summative assessment & WIDA ACCESS 2.0 assessment results in May/June
• Conduct status & growth analyses on summative and EL proficiency assessment results
• June/July 2021
• Finalize report & share findings with DOE leadership & relevant DOE teams to align
findings with DOE supports and guidance
• August 2021
• Share report with policymakers/stakeholders
• Publish report & present findings/DOE’s strategic response

Communication
